title: eriogonum angulosum var. variabile
intro: Eriogonum angulosum var. variabile, commonly known as Desert Buckwheat or Mormon Tea, is a plant species native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. It is a shrubby perennial with small, white or pink flowers, traditionally used as a medicinal plant by Native Americans. The plant has been reported to have various health benefits, including lowering blood sugar levels, reducing inflammation, and acting as an antioxidant. The therapeutic actions of Eriogonum angulosum var. variabile include its anti-diabetic, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties, which are attributed to bioactive constituents such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins.
